\[
\text{Ar–C(=O)OCH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{aqueous-type solvent}]{\text{NaOH}}
\text{Ar–C(=O)O}^- \,(\text{Na}^+)
\]

After the usual acidic workup, this gives the corresponding carboxylic acid:

**Cn1ncc(F)c1-c1cc(C(=O)O)sc1Cl**

Thus, the product retains:

- the N-methyl fluoro-azole ring,
- the chlorothiophene ring,
- the aryl–heteroaryl bond,

and only converts **–CO₂Me → –CO₂H**.

NaOH hydrolyzes the methyl ester group:

\[
\mathrm{-C(=O)OCH_3 \rightarrow -C(=O)OH}
\]

The heteroaryl and chlorothiophene portions remain unchanged. The product is:

**`Cn1ncc(F)c1-c1cc(C(=O)O)sc1Cl`**

Under the basic reaction conditions, the immediate species is the sodium carboxylate; the listed carboxylic acid corresponds to the usual post-reaction workup. This is supported by the exact ORD record and three matching records (source: `call_3wJvElWX0GvFLWVCev1bybwX`).
